facts.fact: Baker McKenzie says Law No. 151 of 2020 is in a one-year compliance grace period that expires on 31 October 2026, by which date all data users must be in full compliance (date is the document's published date).
facts.system: Personal Data Protection Law No. 151 of 2020

facts.fact: Baker McKenzie says the Minister of Telecommunications and Information Technology issued Decree No. 816 of 2025 on 1 November 2025, issuing the Executive Regulations of the PDPL.
facts.system: Personal Data Protection Law No. 151 of 2020

facts.fact: Baker McKenzie says the Personal Data Protection Center (PDPC) officially launched its electronic portal in early October 2026 to receive and process applications for accreditation, licences and permits.
facts.system: Personal Data Protection Law No. 151 of 2020

facts.fact: Baker McKenzie says the PDPC portal also publishes guidelines and frameworks setting out its requirements for controllers and processors; no sanction or decision is reported.
facts.system: Personal Data Protection Law No. 151 of 2020

facts.fact: Baker McKenzie reports the PDPC launched its licensing and permit portal in early October 2026, weeks before the compliance grace period ends.
facts.system: Personal Data Protection Law No. 151 of 2020
